lessons.title: Cloud basics
lessons.lead: Cloud computing means renting computing power, storage and software over the internet instead of buying and running your own hardware. You use what you need, and the provider looks after the physical machines.

cards.title: Pay as you go
cards.manage: pay only for what you use

lessons.analogy: Cloud computing is like getting electricity from the grid: you use what you need, pay for what you use, and never run a power station yourself.

lab.text: Open the Azure portal, click the search bar at the top, and search for "Virtual machines" to see how Azure organizes its services.

lessons.title: Service models
lessons.lead: Every cloud service sits somewhere on a spectrum: how much you manage yourself, and how much Azure manages for you. Know where a service sits and you know what you are responsible for.

cards.title: Platform
cards.manage: you manage: app and data only

cards.title: Software
cards.manage: you manage: just your use of it

lessons.analogy: IaaS is renting an empty plot, PaaS is a furnished flat, and SaaS is a hotel room.

lab.text: Open the Azure portal and find where Virtual Machines and App Service appear in the service list.

lessons.title: Azure regions
lessons.lead: An Azure region is a group of datacenters in one part of the world. Where you place your resources affects speed, cost, availability, and where your data legally lives.

cards.title: Where it runs
cards.manage: a set of datacenters in one area

lessons.analogy: A region is a city. Availability zones are separate neighborhoods with their own power. A region pair is a second city, far enough away to survive a disaster in the first.

lab.text: In the Azure portal, search for "Resource groups", start creating one, and open the Region dropdown to see how many regions Azure offers.

lessons.title: Entra ID
lessons.lead: Microsoft Entra ID is Azure's cloud identity service. For every request it answers two questions: who are you, and what are you allowed to do? It signs people into the Azure portal, Microsoft 365 and many other apps. The sign-in on this very site works on the same idea.
lessons.analogy: Authentication is showing your ID at the door of a building. Authorization is the keycard that decides which rooms you can enter.

lab.text: In the Azure portal, search for "Microsoft Entra ID" and open it. Find your tenant name and open the Users list.
